name: DeepSpeed Inference: Enabling Efficient Inference of Transformer Models at Unprecedented Scale
problem: Inference at model scale needs kernels specialised per model family, and hand-writing them for every architecture does not scale as new transformer variants keep appearing.
mechanism: A kernel JIT library that compiles a specialised inference kernel per model automatically, plus the multi-GPU inference engine built on ZeRO-Inference-style sharding and parameter offloading, so a model far larger than one device's memory can be served with kernels tuned to it.
speedup_reported: NOT RECORDED as a bare multiple. The paper reports large throughput improvements for OPT and other transformer families from its automatic kernel generation, but I did not verify the exact figures with their baselines and settings, and the gain is strongly per-model-family. Also distinguish from the companion arXiv 2401.08671 (DeepSpeed-FastGen), whose abstract does give a figure versus vLLM (2.3x effective throughput).
notes:
Venue verified via Crossref: SC22 (DOI 10.1109/SC41404.2022.00051). Recorded as 'other' because SC/HPC venues are not in the schema enum — the SC22 attribution is here so it is not lost. Adoption in-production: DeepSpeed remains an actively used Microsoft library and MII/DeepSpeed-Inference is deployed, though it has been largely superseded for mainstream LLM serving by vLLM/SGLang/TensorRT-LLM. The kernel-JIT idea is the durable part.
